text.p: Peruvian officials announced on Wednesday the number of people who died as a result of Tuesday's earthquake had reached 13.
The latest deaths to be confirmed included a young girl, Vanessa Duran Espejo, in Ica, 190 miles (305 km) south of Lima, according to Red Cross officials, who did not say how she died.
A man, Efrain Espinoza, also died in Acari, 375 miles (600 km) south of the capital, in the department of Arequipa, according to Teodoro Rojas, govenor of the region.
Two men died in the Leoncio Prado district of Ayacucho, 360 miles (575 km) south of Lima, Pedro Rivera, Ayacucho's Civil Defence coordinator, said without giving more details.

The hardest-hit towns in the earthquake were along the Pacific coast: Nazca, 290 miles (460 km) to the south of the capital Lima, where 300 were injured and Ica, 100 miles (160 km) further north, where another 200 were injured, officials said.
The quake measured 6.4 on the Richter scale and its epicentre was 65 miles (100 km) southeast of Ica, according to Luis Vilca of the Peruvian Geophysic Institute.
Earlier, officials had confirmed the six people died in Nazca, a man in Ica, a woman in Acari and a miner in Moyohauca, 375 miles (600 km) south of Lima.
